defects: Weakens the ring hypothesis from DivisionRing K (gold) to just Semiring R, dropping invertibility of scalars that the theorem needs (a rank-one submodule need not be spanned by an arbitrary nonzero element when scalars aren't invertible)
Weakens AddCommGroup V (gold) to AddCommMonoid M, dropping subtraction/negation needed for the argument

Uses Module.rank (cardinal-valued) instead of finrank (gold's finite natural-number dimension), and combined with the weakened typeclasses the resulting statement is false in general (e.g. R = ℕ, M = ℕ, p = ⊤ has rank 1 but span{2} ≠ ⊤ though 2 ≠ 0 and 2 ∈ p)
Overall not merely a reshaped equivalent — the weakened typeclass assumptions make the produced statement a genuinely different (and false) generalization, not equivalent to the gold
